Reference / web/session

web/session#

Sessions kept on the server, found by a signed cookie (#208):

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let sessions = Sessions(key: secret, store: MemorySessions());

async login(request is WebRequest) is Responding {
    let started = await sessions.started(SessionValue(name: "user", value: name));
    RedirectReply(location: "/", headers: Headers(started.cookie()));
}

async home(request is WebRequest) is Responding {
    let session = await sessions.session(request);   // 401 without one
    TextReply("hi " + session.text("user"));
}

async logout(request is WebRequest) is Responding {
    RedirectReply(location: "/", headers: Headers(await sessions.ended(request)));
}

Description#

Sessions kept on the server, found by a signed cookie (#208):

The cookie (sid unless told) holds a random 256-bit id and its HMAC-SHA256 under key, so an id the server did not give out is refused before the store is asked. The cookie carries the safe defaults of SetCookie (Path=/, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) and Max-Age of the lifetime, 7 days unless told. Around(CsrfProtection(sessions)) makes requests that change state carry the session's csrf() token.

object MemorySessions#

object MemorySessions does SessionStoring

Sessions in the memory of the process: lost when it stops. A session is forgotten lifetime after it was saved; past 10000 sessions the expired ones are dropped on the next save.

object CsrfProtection#

object CsrfProtection does Surrounding

Requests that change state carry the session's token (#208). A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE with a valid session cookie needs an X-CSRF-Token field or, in a urlencoded form, a field csrf equal to session.csrf(); otherwise it is refused with 403. Requests without a session pass: nothing in them acts on a session.

CsrfProtection.CsrfProtection#

CsrfProtection(sessions is Sessions)
